title: Timing lever: word onsets/durations in the sentence model
description: Research 20:15Z (arXiv 2609.40359, PNPL lab): on sub-0 50-word, log inter-onset time ALONE gives 22.9% top-1 BAcc vs real-MEG joint 22.3% (isolated 9.5%); duration~identity r=0.90; ~95% of joint-decoding gain is timing. Holdout gives every word onset (incl OOV) = provided input, not transcripts (organisers call it a shortcut). Champion uses --context.clock order => transformer sees NO timing. 4te.2 tested onset clock only on the obsolete GAP path (tie). Arms: (1) sent40-onset-s0 = --context.clock onset (zero code) vs single band 0.597-0.632 n=2512, bar 0.63+; (2) explicit log next-IOI feature per word; (3) check holdout IOI distribution vs train (HOLDOUT_GAP median 0.21 s) - shift risk, LB transfer is the test. Expected: large if timing transfers (frontier 0.765 plausibly this).
notes: 2026-10-02 20:30Z sent40-onset-s0 (origin sent40-s0, --context.clock onset, seed 0): best sentence-span novel macro 0.609 (n=2512, CI 0.583-0.651) vs order-clock sent40-s0 0.605. Delta +0.004 = noise, below 0.63 bar -> no seeds 1-3, no submission. Early epochs ran ahead (ep7 0.575 vs 0.493) but converged to same level: onset timing speeds learning, adds no ceiling. Not ruled out: onset clock inside MEG-XL encoder / longer spans; holdout gaps differ from train so order clock stays the safe default.

title: Holdout windows from the continuous cache (train/holdout window mismatch)
description: Since 25.9, training and validation windows are gathered from the 50 Hz continuous cache (whole-run resample, demeaned per window). Holdout windows still go through Window(), which resamples each 1 s window on its own, so its first and last 10 samples are edge-distorted and its mean shifts. A model trained on cache windows is scored on differently processed holdout input, so any submission after 25.9 carries a distribution shift that validation cannot see.
acceptance_criteria: Holdout runs are cached the same way: resample_poly over the whole run, fp16. The holdout reader gathers windows through Windows. A test shows holdout and train windows of the same run are processed identically. Window() is deleted if nothing else uses it. Gate: no Kaggle submission from a model trained after 25.9 until this lands.
notes: 05:45Z measured cost of the mismatch: ctx-order40 (trained on old Window) rescored on new continuous Windows, GAP ruler n=1479: 0.5145 vs recorded 0.531 (-0.017). Old models lose ~1.7 pts when fed new-path windows, so holdout for new-path models must use new path too.
close_reason: Merged 3999af8: holdout cached via the training Decimator, windows bit-identical to training's

title: fp16 cache overflow -> inf -> NaN under sensor dropout; ruler scored NaN as perfect
description: sub-0_ses-9_task-Sherlock3_run-1.npz: 291 inf values in 3/3582 windows (fp16 overflow at save). Without augment, Scaler clamp maps inf->5, so it's harmless. With dropout, inf*0=NaN -> loss NaN at epoch 0 (ctx-order-aug40). BalancedTopK: NaN scores give (scores>true).sum()==0, so every word counts as a hit and BAcc=1.0 everywhere. Fix: Epochs saturates to the fp16 max on save+load; BalancedTopK/Ruler count non-finite rows as misses; fit raises on a non-finite loss. Every past augment arm is invalid; rerun aug40.
close_reason: fixed: saturate fp16 cache, non-finite = miss, raise on NaN loss

title: Build continuous 50 Hz cache + all-word sentence spans
description:
MECHANISM (7gf.21 audit, 2026-10-02): holdout sentences are complete text: subj00_holdout01_sentence.npz = 156 sentences, 868 word slots, continuous MEG ~2.5 s each; B (gereonelvers RESULTS.md:18) reports only 451/868 are in-vocab (unverified by us; Kaggle scores in-vocab rows). Our gap check: holdout onset gaps p5/50/95 0.07/0.21/0.57 s vs our vocab-only train spans 0.08/0.29/0.83 (n=70k gaps, 60 runs) = we skip OOV words, holdout does not. Our model trains on vocab-only spans (epochs.py:89 filter, spans.py by onset gap>=0.92 s, chunk 9) so at holdout ~half the context slots are OOV windows it never saw, and local val (vocab-only) is blind to it -> plausible cause of local 0.525 vs LB 0.385. spans.py docstring 'a holdout sentence is a run of vocabulary words only' is WRONG.
DESIGN: (1) cache windows for EVERY word event (label = vocab id or OOV=-1), keep sentence index from PNPL events; (2) spans = PNPL sentences chunked to 9 words, matching holdout; (3) loss on in-vocab slots only (softmax), OOV slots context-only; optional SigLIP to per-word t5 target for OOV slots later (B trains all words); (4) val ruler = in-vocab words of novel all-word sentences (Sherlock1+TheMoth) so it SEES the holdout structure. VRAM: x now ~21 GB fp16 for vocab words; all words ~2x won't fit 32 GB -> OOV windows in pinned CPU RAM (non_blocking per batch) or decimate storage; measure word counts first.
PROOF: local all-word-context novel macro and LB move together; pre-register LB > 0.385 + 0.03.
design: STORAGE (02:45Z): don't cache overlapping windows (all words x 1 s fp16 = 24 GB; x 3 s = 72 GB, too big for VRAM). Cache each run's CONTINUOUS MEG decimated to 50 Hz in fp16 instead: sub-0 ~80 h x 3600 x 50 x 306 x 2 B ~ 8.8 GB; subjects 1-32 add ~2.6 GB. Cut windows on the GPU at batch time by gather (onset index + arange). Window length becomes a free knob (7gf.25.1), and per-window demeaning matches the holdout's Window transform. Events table per run: onset, label (ABSENT for OOV), sentenceidx.
close_reason: Split into megspeech-7gf.25.8 megspeech-7gf.25.9 megspeech-7gf.25.10.

title: Denoising belief LM: span refiner over word-head beliefs, pretrained on external text with simulated MEG confusion
description: Why: lmbound oracle (true neighbours) +.17..+.25 VAL; lmsoft realistic soft-neighbour GPT-2 fusion -.02 (neighbour q(true) .08, OOV neighbours 57-69%). Leaders' lead is subject-agnostic (7gf.114). Not ruled out (lmsoft note): learned end-to-end fusion. Mechanism: our context head learns English only from ~subject-0 training text; a refiner that maps a span of per-word beliefs (50 vocab + OOV) to refined 50-way posteriors can be PRETRAINED on a large external corpus (WikiText-103, no Conan Doyle / no Moth) with beliefs simulated from the base's out-of-fold confusion, then fine-tuned on real cross-fitted (kf5t) MEG beliefs, then applied post-hoc to the blend's Kaggle-span logits. Instrument arm: same refiner with NO text pretraining (MEG-only) - isolates the new information. Pre-reg: VAL (2-fold, like lmsoft) >= base tau-finish +.015 AND local test >= base -.005; else kill this use. Price: build ~agent-hours, train minutes; gain plausible +.02-.05, odds ~25%. Never fit on Kaggle test MEG.
notes:
RESULT 2026-10-10 (commit c568c18 on dev; CLI python -m megspeech.evaluation.studies.wikispans / .lmrefine). VERDICT: pre-reg FAILS -> kill this use (realistic hidden-neighbour refiner). Harness check PASSES (oracle).
Setup: base m11xsp7hub6d2v3 (VAL .6537 n 1296/1216; local test .6970 n 1358/775). OOF beliefs: NO m11x OOF exists -> used closest consistent base, peer dump peerbase-s0 (kf5t-f0..4 on held-out subject-0 training sessions, 765k rows); folds 0-3 train + fill the simulation bank, fold 4 = watched (base CE 2.409). "rebased" = same ruler with peerbase's own val beliefs as base (.6415). WikiText-103 train: 29,216 articles kept, 229 dropped naming Sherlock/Conan Doyle/The Moth; 10.68M spans / 81.1M words, in-vocab .332 (MEG ~.40). Spans cut by the training rule Spans.by_sentence, NOT the Kaggle histogram (no Kaggle-row adaptation). Simulated belief = a real OOF row of the same label (OOV rows: any OOV row). Refiner 3x128 transformer, residual on own log-probs (untrained = identity). Scoring = lmsoft 2-fold VAL crossfit + local-test transfer, refined-minus-base as the fused channel. Two runs: p1 (1 pass stage 1, stage 1 selected on REAL watched fold) and h20000-p0.25 (0.25 pass, stage 1 selected on 20k held-out SIMULATED spans). Fine-tune 40 epochs x2 lrs, best epoch on watched.
NULL: identity refiner (p1 hidden/text-only = untouched) scores VAL -.009 [-.019,-.000] -> the crossfit itself costs ~.009 on this ruler; read VAL deltas against it.
HIDDEN (realistic), VAL d [CI] | local test d [CI]  (S1 / Moth VAL):
 p1 text        -.009 [-.021,+.002] | -.020 [-.039,-.008]  (-.006/-.013)
 p1 meg-only    -.008 [-.019,+.001] | -.018 [-.036,-.007]  (-.005/-.011)
 held text-only -.010 [-.025,+.006] | +.012 [-.015,+.028]
 held text      -.008 [-.021,+.008] | -.008 [-.023,+.003]  (-.012/-.004)
 held meg-only  -.005 [-.017,+.005] | -.013 [-.041,-.001]
 Watched CE: base 2.409 -> text 2.376/2.369, meg-only 2.376 (-.03-.04 nats, overfits after ~2-4 epochs). Rebased VAL all within [-.013,+.004].
ORACLE harness (true neighbours one-hot, target hidden), VAL | local test:
 p1 text-only +.058 [+.031,+.088] | +.083 ; p1 text +.120 [+.093,+.152] | +.128 ; p1 meg-only +.080 [+.055,+.111] | +.096
 held text-only +.035 | +.047 ; held text +.092 [+.063,+.128] | +.123 ; held meg-only +.109 [+.076,+.139] | +.121
 -> recovers MORE than lmbound oracle backoff/pmi (+.044) and ~= pmi-right (+.091): the refiner+ruler+crossfit path fires. Stage 1 alone transfers under oracle (+.035..+.058 with zero MEG fine-tuning); pretrain-then-finetune vs meg-only is +.040 (p1) and -.017 (held): not separable, mixed sign.
What fired: simulated pretraining under HIDDEN does not transfer to real beliefs: real watched CE of the stage-1 model 2.70-2.78 vs 2.409 identity at every check (p1 kept identity); the held-selected stage-1 model is neutral on VAL. Fine-tuning learns -.03 nats CE that does not survive the ruler.
Not ruled out: (1) a sampler with correlated draws - independent per-word draws ignore that the base context head already used context (double counting) and that OOV draws ignore word identity; (2) a true m11x OOF (refiner trained on peerbase beliefs, applied to the sharper m11x ensemble -> local-test transfer -.01..-.02 is plausibly that shift); (3) a corpus with MEG-text label prior/OOV share; (4) larger MEG fine-tune data (kf5t only covers subject-0 train). Oracle numbers bound what correct neighbours are worth (+.09..+.12), so the gap is entirely neighbour belief quality.

title: V1 instrument: 50x50 RSA of each teacher vs our MEG model's confusion matrix (CPU)
description: Cheapest ranking for view 1. From a trained Deep model's val/local-test predictions build the 50x50 confusion (or mean-softmax) matrix; for each candidate teacher build the 50x50 cosine matrix of its type-level word vectors; Spearman RSA (upper triangle) + bootstrap CI over words. A teacher whose geometry already matches what MEG confuses is a target the encoder can reach; one that separates what MEG cannot is wasted capacity. Also report: teacher's own 50-way separability (min pairwise distance). Teachers: current t5-large h12 type-avg, wav2vec2-xlsr type-avg, whisper-medium L8-24 type-avg, HuBERT-ll60k, EmbeddingGemma2 word at 768/256/128, PanPhon-feature vectors, one-hot (null). Minutes on CPU once vectors exist. Gate for V1 training runs: run only teachers with RSA CI above one-hot/t5.

title: Safe target-encoder alternatives: matched-complexity (50 words) vs full-complexity (all words, context)
description:
Owner ask 2026-10-07 22:18 Sofia. Two views on what the MEG encoder should regress onto.
VIEW 1 MATCH COMPLEXITY: the scored task is 50 words; 50 points span <=49 dims, so at the 50-word level any teacher reduces to its 50x50 similarity geometry. Pick the geometry MEG can actually separate, small dims, no context.
VIEW 2 FULL COMPLEXITY: supervise every heard word (in/out of 50) with contextual, layer-chosen audio/text states; more signal per window, rich axes the aux terms already show help (syn05/nbr03/ac03 kept).
Not mutually exclusive: view-2 teachers as aux losses, view-1 geometry as the head target.
SAFE = weights under an OSI-approved licence, per rules.md 6c: 'only use open source code licensed under an Open Source Initiative-approved license ... that in no event limits commercial use'. Apache-2.0 / MIT / BSD = safe. CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA, PDDL = not OSI, flagged unclear (our reading, not a rule line). NC (mms-1b, SONAR) excluded. Licences from research/2026-10-07_target_encoders.md (HF cardData, queried 2026-10-07).
Contextual LM targets (gpt2, Qwen3) stay owner-gated; listed only as gated.
Ranking instrument for both views: megspeech-7gf.137 (alignment study) + the 50x50 RSA child below. Related bug: 7gf.138.

title: Broad: subject-count scaling curve (does held-out-subject score saturate in N subjects?)
description: Idea: each training subject adds an independent direction of inter-subject variability; a new (0%/25%-group) subject is decoded well only if it falls in the span. If the held-out-subject curve vs N training subjects is still rising at N=32, more subjects (MASC 27, Gwilliams, Armeni via DUA) is the Broad lever, and eventually wants a bigger shared model + per-subject layer. If flat, subjects are not the bottleneck. Deep is a different question: attribution (efd) shows subj0 fine-tune overwrites MASC pretraining. Instrument: Deep-pretrained encoder + subject layer, train on N in {4,8,16,32} Broad subjects (ses-11), score held-out subjects ses-12, 2 seeds at the ends. Price ~4 short runs x ~40 min GPU; P(curve still rising) ~0.5; informs whether to spend ct5/7gf.133 data work. Relates 7gf.132, ct5.

title: kcut ruler not Kaggle-faithful for windows >1s: bound at sentence end, no isolated 1s word trials
description: Audit 2026-10-07: under --grouping kaggle each word window is bounded at its whole PNPL sentence end+1s (run_cache.py:144-152,187-188; grouping.py:57-66), not its ~5.5-word piece end like Kaggle epochs (kaggle.py:122). Isolated words (NO_SENTENCE) get continuous MEG, Kaggle gives 1s epochs. Zero-tail share at 1.5s: local 6.6% vs Kaggle ~28%. Inflates any window>1s model (w15 kcut .6206/.6955). Fix: under KAGGLE bound each word at its piece's last word end+TAIL (piece-level stop/opening), plus deal a Kaggle-sized share of words as lone 1s epochs. Oracle: 1.0s-window model score unchanged (bit-equal domains when window<=1s for in-piece words); zero-tail share at 1.5s within a few pct of 28%.
notes:

Isolated 1s epochs not simulated (remaining ~5pt). words.tsv got a finish column (backups words.pre_finish.tsv). Rescore queued: ctrl s0/s1/s2, w15 s1/s2.

title: Cross-fitted KD: teacher distributions on training words from folds that never trained on them
description: 7gf.128 gap locator: on training spans teachers score fit .776 with MEG share .22-.24 vs val .08 - they memorise training MEG. Current KD (--optim.teacher, megspeech/training/teacher.py) reads the teacher's distribution on every labelled TRAINING word, i.e. memorised, overconfident targets -> mechanism for kd05u null (.6527). Fix: K-fold over training sessions, each fold's teacher scores only its held-out fold, student distils toward these out-of-fold distributions (stacking / cross-fitting). title: Channel-first word encoder: one shared temporal encoder per sensor, spatial fusion after (time first, space second)
description: Owner idea 2026-10-06. Physics: MEG quasi-static, sensor_i(t)=sum_k L_ik s_k(t), real gains incl sign, no propagation lag; ~80 SSS dims over 306 sensors. Today ConvWords mixes space FIRST (1x1 Conv1d 306->256, conv.py:75-79) then dilated temporal blocks. Arm: reshape [b,306,t]->[b*306,1,t], shared small temporal stack (DilatedBlock, hidden h~32, same dilations/kernels), plus learned per-sensor embedding (or SpatialAttention Fourier position features), then fuse [b,306*h,t] -> hidden via 1x1 conv, then existing pool/head. Mechanisms: (a) 306x more sequences for the temporal encoder via weight sharing, (b) per-channel augmentation becomes meaningful (no neighbour shortcut before fusion), (c) inference: time courses transfer across subjects better than lead fields, so a later per-subject fusion layer targets the Deep->Broad loss (us 6.9pt vs leaders 3.6, 7gf.114). Cost ~5x the temporal FLOPs of today at h=32. Plausible size unknown; architecture tier. PRIOR ART IN REPO: MEG-XL (7gf.5) is per-channel tokenised + criss-cross, frozen read 0.366 vs conv 0.623 - but its word feature was a MEAN OVER CHANNELS x tokens; sensors carry sign-mirrored copies of each source, so a channel mean cancels them (suspected harness flaw, unverified). Gate: ema-cd25 recipe, origin sent40-ioi-ema9998-s0, seed 1, vs ema-cdrop25-s1 on val + Kaggle-cut local test (ruler per 7gf.105); +1.5 to keep. Proof the change landed: parameter count and a unit test that permuting sensors before the temporal stack permutes nothing it should not (temporal stack is channel-equivariant).

title: Prioritised sampler: per-span visibility (seen count) x difficulty (EMA loss), unseen first
description: Owner design 2026-10-06: every span carries visibility (times drawn) and difficulty (EMA of its training loss). Unseen spans weigh heaviest by default (prior = max difficulty, as prioritized replay gives new transitions max priority, Schaul et al. 2016); once seen, weight tilts by difficulty (Loshchilov & Hutter 2015 online batch selection). w = base * (1+seen)^-beta * (loss/mean)^gamma, floor so easy spans never starve. Difficulty from TRAINING loss only. Read runs never above their natural weight (standing rule). Plugs into megspeech.training.sampling.curriculum as a Curriculum (weights/observe). Extends 7gf.84 Robust (strata-level, null 1 seed). Also: Sherlock is ~85% of subj0 words - visibility decay naturally rotates through it. Test: 1 arm vs E0 single (val .6413 / test .6722), then Broad arm vs bgmix05-s0.
notes:
Lit caveat: high-loss-first hurts on noisy data (Mindermann 2022 RHO-LOSS: highest loss often unlearnable/noisy; Swayamdipta 2020 data maps: hard-to-learn = mislabelled, ambiguous helps most; self-paced easy-first Kumar 2010). MEG single trials are noise-dominated and the field rejects bad epochs (autoreject, Jas 2017). Plan: arms priority +1 AND -1 with visibility 1, plus visibility-only. Better difficulty = reducible loss (loss minus a reference model's), RHO-style; follow-up if the sign test shows signal. Citations from memory, verify before README.
BGMix clash (owner 2026-10-06): with bgmix a span's loss is measured on template + ANOTHER trial's residual, so its difficulty mixes its own noise with a donor's. Order: test on Deep first (no bgmix, clean). For Broad: update difficulty only from un-mixed draws (needs the mixed mask passed to observe), or drop difficulty and keep visibility only. Possible synergy: data-map bad trials excluded as bgmix donors.
Owner 2026-10-06: don't collapse the spectrum to 0/+-1 - arms changed to visibility 0.5, priority 0/+0.5/-0.5 (power 1 risks floor/ceiling saturation = binary-ish). Logging weight quantiles, clamp shares and ESS per epoch to verify the fluidity. Next: mastery-driven continuous power schedule (_curriculum_scale analogue) instead of a fixed power.

Features into the 6ow booster (peer.py/boosted.py): predicted surprisal for words i-1, i and i+1, alongside the existing timing (duration, IOI, position, span length).

title: Null autopsy: pretrained-teacher nulls (7gf.37/.40/.41/.54/.101) never diagnosed
description:
Owner 2026-10-05: teacher-target nulls were closed after one single-seed run each, mechanism never found. Reopen each. Harness suspects to verify per run:
(1) TARGET ANISOTROPY: 6ow found GPT-2 targets mean-norm/std 15.4, top-5 dims hold 86% variance. Did 7gf.37/.54/.101 whiten? If not, cosine/SigLIP loss mostly fit the shared mean and outlier dims, so the word content barely reached the gradient.
(2) WRONG READER: 6ow's own-task checker read ~0.25 on the base encoder (true ~0.75) until switched from ridge-to-centroid to a trained probe. Were earlier own-task or probe verdicts read the same way?
(3) NOISE: deltas 0.6147-0.6263 vs 0.6205 and 0.6383 vs 0.6445 sit inside the seed sd (~0.014) on a per-seed max-over-epochs ruler (see memory best-epoch-bias). These were undetectable, not refuted.
(4) JOINT TRAINING: the aux weight competes with the 50-way loss, and no weight sweep or schedule was tried. Check whether the aux loss even fell.
(5) TARGET FIT: probe R2 is about 0.01, so most of each teacher's variance is invisible from MEG. Test reduced-rank / CCA targets (only the teacher directions MEG can predict), and teacher-as-soft-label (50-word semantic similarity as label smoothing).
(6) COVERAGE: teachers supervise ALL words (~15x more supervised rows than the 50-way loss). Check whether the runs used that or only target words.
Theory: all experts share one MEG input, so a gain comes from steering the encoder to features the 50-way loss misses, with ensemble-like diversity. Not from new input information. Plausible size: ensemble-scale, +1-2 pt.
Deliverable: per null, a verdict of harness bug / undetectable / mechanism-refuted, with evidence. Cheap first: grep each run config for whitening, aux weight and coverage, then re-run the best candidate with fixes and 3 seeds.

title: Joint fine-tune of the experts: one model, each expert CNN reading its own crop of a shared window
description: Owner call 2026-10-04: fine-tune the expert sub-models jointly instead of stacking frozen embeddings. title: K-fold cross-fit ensemble: rotate held-out sessions, ensemble all fold models
description: Owner idea 2026-10-04. Split subject-0 training sessions into K stratified folds (Stratify generalised from 3 partitions to K balanced groups). Fold model k trains on the other K-1 and picks its epoch on fold k (test share 0). Submission = ensemble of the K fold models, which replaces the seed ensemble at the same GPU cost (6 seeds -> 6 folds); every session is trained on by K-1 models. Gains: (1) every session is used for training in the final ensemble, with no blind fixed-epoch refit; (2) out-of-fold predictions cover 100% of the sessions: a ruler K times bigger, and the held-out inputs for the expert stacker (7gf.77). Caveat: the fold that picks the epoch also scores it, a small optimistic bias; report it beside the official-val score. Test: 6-fold ensemble vs 6-seed ens-strat on official val (n=2512).

title: Instrument: LM fusion oracle bound (true left context) on val, TheMoth read separately
description: 7gf.6 gate (single-word top-1 > 0.5) was mis-set for BAcc@10: fusion only has to lift the true word into top-10. Instrument: on val spans, log p_LM(word | TRUE preceding words) over the 868-class vocab from a small pretrained causal LM (GPT-2 class), fused as logits + lambda*logp, lambda on a grid; report macro BAcc@10 per domain at n=2512. Upper bound (teacher-forced context; real decoding needs beam search over the predicted words). Kill if bound < +0.015 on TheMoth. HAZARD: Sherlock public domain -> LM may have memorised it, inflating Sherlock1 and amounting to exploiting holdout source text; TheMoth is the clean read; any submission needs an owner rules decision (human). Price ~1 h code + minutes GPU; plausible gain at bound 0.02-0.08.
close_reason: Killed before running (design flaw found in audit): the 50 classes are function words, and on holdout most neighbouring words are OOV with unknown identity, so a teacher-forced LM bound is unreachable. The reachable version (LM over in-vocab slots, OOV as wildcards) is the word-order/co-occurrence prior the context model already learns from training text (zero-MEG ctx 0.33). Price ~1h for ~0 expected gain. Not ruled out: a decoder of OOV word classes (length/POS) feeding an LM.

title: Add MEG-XL backbone fine-tune path
description: MIT, ~567 MB weights into DataRoot.foreign('MEG-XL'). README asks 40-80 GiB; test bf16 / grad-checkpoint / smaller batch on the 5090.
design: DESIGN 2026-10-02 20:22Z. HOLDOUT CONSTRAINT (probed subj00 archives): 156 sentence epochs, 868 words, each epoch STARTS at first word onset (0 s pre-onset), ends 1.02-1.36 s (p0/p50) after last onset, median length 2.5 s; plus 92 isolated 1 s word epochs. MEG-XL's own recipe (3 s per word from -0.5 s, baseline first 0.5 s, concatenated) is NOT reproducible at holdout. Adaptation: feed each span's CONTINUOUS segment [first onset, last onset + 1.0 s] at our 50 Hz cache, padded to the batch max; isolated words = 1 s segment. Train segments cut identically (no pre-onset, same tail) so train/holdout match. Trunk out [B,C,T/12,512] = 240 ms tokens; word feature = mean over channels x tokens covering [onset, onset+0.5 s] -> MLP -> context width, replacing WordNet slots in SentenceNet (strategy: ContextConfig.encoder = conv|megxl). Scaling: per-segment RobustScaler per channel + clip 5 (also 4te.10's normalisation). PLUMBING: external/MEG-XL has no pyproject -> committed fetch step (git clone + checkout 97da041) and importlib load with sys.path; optional extra megxl = pytorch-lightning, einops (only third-party deps of trunk+BioCodec); deptry DEP002 ignore with reason. GATE before training: VRAM/throughput probe on the 5090 at batch of 64 spans x <=10 s, bf16 + checkpointing; GPU currently busy (onset arm + Broad seeds).
notes:
20:20Z AUDIT external/MEG-XL @97da041: model brainstorm/models/criss_cross_transformer.py:15 CrissCrossTransformerModule(Lightning); forward(raw_meg[B,C,T], sensor_xyz, sensor_abc, sensor_type, sensor_mask, apply_mask=False) -> [B,C,T/12,512]. Ckpt = full Lightning ckpt, 26.0M params incl frozen BioCodec tokenizer (3.2M, 12x downsample, 6 RVQ x 256). Load: build tokenizer, Module(tokenizer, **hparams) (v2: pop debug_nan_checks), drop rope_embedding_layer.rotate keys, strict=False. Inputs 50 Hz; per word 3 s window from onset-0.5, baseline-sub first 0.5 s, RobustScaler per channel (mag/grad), clip +-5, then concatenated (50 words=150 s, batch 1). Sensor xyz/abc/type from meg_sensors_information.json, centred+scaled. Their FT: SigLIP to T5-large L12, trunk lr 1e-5 head 1e-3, bf16, README 80 GB. Word embedding: tokens start//12..ceil(end/12), mean over time -> [306,512] flattened -> MLP 2048 -> 1024. Deps for trunk: torch, pytorch_lightning, einops. Plan for 5090 (32 GB): sentence-length segments (<=9 words x 3 s = 27 s -> ~113 tokens) instead of 150 s, bf16, grad checkpointing; softmax head on our ruler. Concatenated windows overlap => carries timing like 4te.9.

Quasi-static field gives sign-mirrored copies of each source on opposite sensors, so a channel mean cancels most of the signal - could explain frozen 0.366 vs conv 0.623 independently of MEG-XL's quality. 5.2 channel-resolved PCA16 is the partial counter-test. title: OVMI auxiliary loss: batch soft-confusion mutual information under SUBTLEX prior
description: Owner ask 2026-10-08. OVMI = competition auxiliary metric (ruler.py:124 Ruler.information: plug-in MI word vs top-1 prediction, confusion rows weighted by prior renormalised over present classes). Spec: optim.mi: float = 0.0 weight; per batch over labelled words, soft joint J = onehot(y)^T softmax(context logits)/n, rows reweighted by the same prior Ruler.information uses; loss = -mi * MI_bits(J). 0 creates nothing. Test arm: one seed w1.0, sent40-masc27 warm, mi 0.1, vs ema-cd25-masc27w-s3. Bar +.015 val; predicted null-to-small (overlaps optim.balance, qr2).
notes:

title: Per-label ensemble weights (shrunk), cross-fit on Broad ruler subjects
description: Owner idea 2026-10-08: weight ensemble members per label by their per-label performance instead of one global weight (Blended.weights = member counts today, megspeech/evaluation/blended.py). Risk: K members x ~250 labels free weights from ~2.5k val words (median ~13 words/label/domain) = overfit. Design: per-label weight w[m,l] = softmax(beta * shrunk_score[m,l]), shrunk_score = (n_l*s[m,l] + k*s[m,global])/(n_l+k), k and beta chosen on fit half only. Proof (no leakage): Broad ruler (32 subjects, 25k words) split by SUBJECT into halves A/B; fit weights on A, score B, and swap; compare 2-fold mean vs uniform blend of the same members on the same halves. Members: the xc5w6 set (bens4.sh X+WA+WS). Bar: +.015 abs on held-out halves; directional below. CPU only (--device cpu). title: Share the GPU data cache across training lanes
description: Each training process loads its own ~9.4 GB cuda cache of the same continuous MEG (log: 'cache 9.43 GB on cuda'). Two lanes = 2 copies = ~19 GB of 31.5 GB; adding MEG-XL pushed VRAM to 31.6 GB and spilled into shared memory (thrash, owner saw 65% util, 2026-10-07 11:35). Options: one process training two configs, CUDA IPC shared tensor from a cache server, or fp16/decimated cache. Gain: ~9 GB headroom, so lanes can run bigger models with VRAM near half. Owner gauge: bd memory gpu-efficiency-gauge.
notes: 2026-10-07 11:50 Sofia, design notes. Now: each lane loads every run whole onto the GPU as one float16 continuous signal (cache 9.43 GB on cuda) and windows come from on-device gathers. Disk is read only at startup. No rotation. Options: (a) CUDA IPC sharing between processes. torch documents CUDA IPC as Linux-only, so it does not work on native Windows (not verified for WSL2). (b) Host-resident path: np.load(mmap_mode='r') on the cache .npy, so the OS page cache dedups across lanes for free. Gather on CPU, pin, then .to(cuda, non_blocking) with prefetch on a side stream. A batch is a few MB, so PCIe is no bottleneck; CPU gather throughput is the risk. 94 GB RAM total, ~42 GB free. (c) Two models in one process sharing one device tensor; lanes coupled, ugly. Recommend (b) behind a strategy flag (resident=gpu|host); gate it on matched epoch time. Gain = ~9 GB VRAM per lane = headroom for bigger runs (MEG-XL batch 16), not a 3rd lane (owner cap stays at 2).

title: High-gamma spatial filters before envelope: xDAWN-on-envelope and template LCMV, k-channel probe
description: 7gf.80 took the sensor envelope and then mixed it, which loses local high-gamma (HG) because power is nonlinear. Spatial filtering has to come BEFORE the power step. Probe (CPU, the same LDA as 7gf.80, compared to the sensor-envelope .2315): HG 70-120 Hz from the 250 Hz source data, then spatial filters, then log-envelope at 50 Hz, then LDA alone and fused with the low band. Filters: (a) xDAWN on the HG ENVELOPE, locked to word onsets only (no word identity), fit on the TRAINED partition; HG is not phase-locked, so raw-signal xDAWN would fail, which is why the filters are fit on the envelope. Sweep k=1,2,4,8,16; choose k where the generalized eigenvalue falls to the shuffled-onset level. (b) Template fsaverage LCMV, ROI virtual channels (bilateral STG, IFG, ventral motor). (c) Sensor envelope as control. Gate: the best k beats .2315 by a clear margin AND the envelope positive control passed; only then build the learned arm (band-pass, learned 306->k spatial layer, square/log/downsample, appended as extra input channels). Runs after the envelope agent af5a8aa01efeb7a1f.
design: PLAN (owner 2026-10-06): classify standalone first, then late fusion. S1 CPU: add a Projection strategy to studies/envelope.py (pca=current | xdawn-on-envelope | lcmv later), HG bands 70-95 + 105-120 (skip the 100 Hz harmonic), same LDA harness; controls = PCA projection, shuffled onsets, xDAWN topographies (edge sensors => muscle). LCMV only if xDAWN shows signal. S2 decisive and cheap: logit fusion log p_net + w*log p_HG against the trained model's saved probs.pt (telemetry); w chosen on VAL; report local test. Gate +1.5 local test. S3 only if S2 passes: precompute an HG log-envelope k-channel cache at 50 Hz, small conv branch giving a word embedding, fused before the heads, with modality dropout; one GPU arm. Odds: S1 shows signal ~25%; S2 clears given S1 ~20%; overall ~5%. Cost S1 ~3 h agent + 1 h CPU, S2 minutes, S3 ~4 h + 1-2 h GPU.
notes: 2026-10-06 decisions: (1) Beamform ONLY the high band. Low band: a beamformer is a fixed linear sensor mix the net already learns, so it adds no information for Deep (≈0 expected); its one real use is a shared source space across subjects for Broad, owner-gated, parked. High band: power is nonlinear, so the spatial filter has to come before the envelope. (2) Correction: the rebuilt envelope study (7gf.80, agent af5a8aa01efeb7a1f) already projects before the envelope, but onto the top-POWER components of the band covariance, which at high band is mostly muscle and noise. xDAWN-on-envelope targets word-locked SNR instead; the difference is the objective, not the order. (3) Channels: few (4-8), k chosen from the generalized eigenvalue against a shuffled-onset control, because 7gf.80 concatenation cost -2.1 pt. (4) Gain = new information only (the band is discarded today); the risk is overfitting the weak input, hence modality dropout in S3. Lit: ECoG HG standard; EEG HG + low frequencies helps some subjects (Synigal 2020, PMC7200998); MEG HG works only with beamformer/source space + coarse classes (PLOS CB 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1005938; Sci Rep s41598-017-14452-3); LibriBrain nulls: MEGConformer band study, arXiv 2604.04129. Waits on: envelope agent high-band result (running).

description: megspeech/evaluation/rulers/deep.py:21-24 prints 'novel-text macro X over N words' = unweighted mean of report.domains[*].novel.bacc10 over ALL val domains. Fix: print it at macro.tau over counted domains only, or drop it; never quote it as a score.

title: Colored brain-noise augmentation (subject noise model, p=0.5)
description:
Owner idea 2026-10-05. Model subj0 background activity as a distribution and inject fresh draws per sentence or word, p=0.5.
Why not remove-then-replace: single-trial SNR is tiny (probe R2 ~0.01). A trial is mostly background, so subtracting estimated noise leaves only the word's average template and discards within-word variation. So ADD fresh noise instead.
Noise model, fitted on TRAINING runs only, sampled on GPU:
(a) Gaussian with the subject's sensor covariance x 1/f spectrum: sample white, colour by the spectrum, mix by the covariance Cholesky.
(b) Real background: windows from inter-sentence silences.
Scale alpha so SNR drops by a set dB; sweep 2 values.
Prior art: 7gf.92 BGMix (add a shifted other window, mix 0.5) scored 0.6396 vs 0.6445, single seed, null; additive noise was never tested (7gf.18 close note). Expected small, +0-1 pt.
Cost: one sent40 run ~6 min, 2 seeds per arm. Gate: official val vs the sent40-ioi-ema9998 seed band; keep at +0.015. Also try as an ensemble member (diversity).
notes: Owner 2026-10-05: derive noise as trial - word template (signal/noise split). Templates via rERP regression (deconvolve word overlap), CROSS-FITTED (in-sample residuals shrink by 1-1/n). Outputs: per-word held-out template R2 (signal share), noise-cov homogeneity across words (pooled vs per-word sampler), matched-filter expert scores, swap-residual augmentation. Depends on 6yl.

title: Evoked-reproducibility spatial denoiser (DSS / xDAWN) fitted on subj0 training data
description: Owner 2026-10-05: use the deep subject's hours to denoise. Fit spatial filters on TRAINING runs only that maximise word-locked reproducibility: DSS (de Cheveigne & Simon 2008) or xDAWN (Rivet 2009, the P300-BCI workhorse). Project every window, train and test alike, onto the top-k components. Single fixed operator; no fitting on test MEG (test adaptation is forbidden). Per-word denoising is impossible at test (the word is unknown), so per-word averages may serve only as a training target (single-trial to word-average evoked as an aux/expert). First audit what spatial preprocessing the base already does (whitened comps?) and whether its learned spatial layer already subsumes this. Cheap check: LDA instrument raw vs DSS-projected, then a base retrain if it moves.

title: 125 Hz cache: does 25-60 Hz (low gamma) carry word evidence a trained model can use
description: Current pipeline decimates 250->50 Hz, keeping <25 Hz (constants.py:15). Gross 2013 (PLoS Biol) found speech-locked low gamma 25-40 Hz in MEG; the 40 Hz ASSR is strong in MEG. Our high-band instrument (30-120 Hz envelope LDA 0.2315 vs low 0.3247) had no positive control and was linear. Test: cache at decimate 2 (125 Hz, <62 Hz), retrain the base. Blocker: the frozen BioCodec trunk assumes 50 Hz input (trunk.py:3), so this needs a rate-agnostic front end or a dual-band input (50 Hz trunk + 25-60 Hz band-power branch). Cost: ~2.5x per epoch. Prior: low, maybe +0.5 pt. Gate: official val, 3 seeds, vs sent40 base.
notes: Envelope study rebuilt + low-band positive control (4-8/8-13/13-25 Hz) delegated: Sonnet agent, worktree branch envelope, CPU only.

title: Deconvolved per-word MEG templates (rERP) as expert
description:
Owner-approved 2026-10-05. Per-word evoked templates fitted jointly by regression (rERP, Smith & Kutas 2015) so neighbour-word overlap cancels; a plain average is smeared by ~300 ms word spacing. Score each test window by its whitened match to each of the 50 templates; feed the match scores (word i, i+/-1) to the 6ow booster. Fit on training runs only.
Prior: LDA is already whitened template matching and the span transformer already does learned deconvolution, so expect +0-0.5 pt. Expert-only value, through decorrelation. Gate: fused score vs the 0.6475 control, 3 seeds, keep at +0.015. Run after the surprisal expert (higher odds).
notes: Also emit cross-fitted residuals + held-out template R2 per word + residual covariance per word, for kic noise model and a matched-filter expert.

title: Hierarchical head: factor the 50-way word logits through the part-of-speech head
description: Owner idea (2026-10-04): classify the part of speech first, then the vocabulary word within it. Factorised: log p(w) = log p(tag(w)) + log p(w | tag), where the 17-way POS head trains on EVERY heard window (in- and out-of-vocabulary, ~2.5x the 50-way labels) and the 50-way head adds a within-tag term. The 50 fall into ~10 classes (AUX 12, PRON 10, ADP 7, DET 6, ADV 4), so a correct tag narrows the choice to ~5-12 words. Gate: run only if 7gf.93's aux arm shows the POS head decodes above its prior (log its held-out POS accuracy / balanced accuracy vs the tag-frequency baseline). Mechanism risk: the 50-head already learns its own words' POS implicitly; the gain must come from the extra OOV windows sharpening the content/function split. Training-only target; no holdout text.

title: Instrument: high-gamma envelope (>25 Hz) - does it carry word evidence the 0-25 Hz trunk lacks
description: Cheap CPU gate before any trunk change. Physics: high-gamma (70-150 Hz) envelope tracks local cortical firing and carries speech information in ECoG; in MEG it is weak but non-zero (sensor-level, temporal). Our trunk reads the cached signal; first establish what band the cache keeps (sampling rate, any low-pass). If content >25 Hz exists: per-word features = log envelope of band-passed bands (e.g. 30-45, 55-95, 105-125 Hz if Nyquist allows) binned over 0-0.8 s, same LDA harness as 7gf.69 (train subj 0 Deep train, novel-span words of Sherlock1 n=1296 + TheMoth n=1216). Judge: alone vs the 7gf.69 low-band LDA (0.325 macro) and the union of their top-10 hits (unique hits vs ctx head). Bar to promote to a trunk input: unique hits not already covered by the context head that could plausibly move macro >=1.5pt. Not ruled out by 7gf.69 (that tested only the low band).
notes:
INSTRUMENT RESULT 2026-10-04 (CPU only): the >25 Hz band adds NO per-word evidence. Null. Nothing committed.
Source check: the cache is 50 Hz (resample_poly /5, anti-alias < 25 Hz), but the h5 source is 250 Hz, band-passed 0.1-125 Hz, so the question can be asked. Per-band covariance spectra are non-degenerate to ~80 comps (eig/eig0 at 80: 1.5e-3, at 100: 4e-5).
Features: subj 0 h5 at 250 Hz, x1e12 -> per band (30-45, 55-95, 105-120 Hz; 50/100 Hz line avoided) train-fit band covariance (16 strided train runs) -> whitened top-80 comps -> butter4 sosfiltfilt -> |hilbert| -> log -> per-run z-score per comp -> 8 x 0.1 s bin means over 0-0.8 s after onset = 3x80x8 = 1920 dims. Same word rows as 7gf.69 (order asserted equal: train 307,335 labelled words / 156 runs subj 0; Sherlock1 ses-11 run-2, TheMoth ses-29 run-1). Windows NOT cut at sentence bounds (7gf.69's were). No ses-11/12 of subj 1-32, no holdout, no .fif, no GPU.
Harness = 7gf.69: PCA dim on inner fold (every 10th train run, uniform-prior LW-shrinkage LDA), novel-span BAcc@10. Low band reproduced exactly: S1 0.3482 / Moth 0.3012 / macro 0.3247.
High PCA is near-isotropic (50% var @645 dims, 90% @1519). Inner fold BAcc@10 at 645/1007/1216/1519/1710/1876 dims: .204/.206/.199/.203/.203/.203 - chance for top-10 of 50 is 0.20. Chose 1007 (shrink .005).
(a) High alone, novel spans: S1 0.2463 (n=1296), Moth 0.2166 (n=1216), macro 0.2315 (chance 0.20; low band 0.3247).
(b) Low+high concat LDA (low 631 PCs + high 645 PCs, inner-picked; inner .306 vs low-alone .338 in 7gf.69): S1 0.3692, Moth 0.2376, macro 0.3034 - WORSE than low alone (-2.1pt): the high dims add noise.
(c) Top-10 hits not in ctx (ens-kdn12 context head, tau .5; ctx hits S1 1098/1296, Moth 911/1216): high 37 / 67, low 41 / 62, concat 40 / 71. High-only vs (ctx or low): 30 / 58. CAUTION: a chance-level top-10 ranker gets ~0.2 x ctx misses = ~40 (S1) / ~61 (Moth) such hits, so both the high AND the low counts sit at the random expectation - unique-hit counts are not evidence at this accuracy. Corr of true-class log-prob: high-low 0.04/-0.02, high-ctx 0.05/0.07.
(d) Fusion ctx(tau .5)+w*high(uniform prior): w.1 S1 +0.0023 Moth -0.0088 macro -0.0032; w.2 -0.0111; w.3 -0.0084. Cross-picked (w<=.3): pick S1 w.25 -> Moth -0.0221; pick Moth w0 -> S1 0; macro -0.0111. Bootstrap macro w.1 -0.0032 [-0.0125,+0.0067], w.25 -0.0070 [-0.0190,+0.0048]. Concat member: cross-picked -0.0065, w.1 bootstrap -0.0049 [-0.0149,+0.0058].
Mechanism check (instrument, not just the score): onset-locked grand mean of the z-scored log-envelope, RMS over 80 comps per bin, vs SE ~0.0011: 30-45 Hz 0.0018 -> 0.0035 (slight rise over 0.8 s), 55-95 Hz flat 0.0016-0.0019, 105-120 Hz flat 0.0021-0.0026. Between/within class variance ratio per feature 0.00016-0.00018 vs chance 0.000159 in all bands and bins. So no word-locked high-gamma response is visible at this sensor/component level, not just a classifier failure.
NOT tested: no positive control of the envelope pipeline on a known-responsive band (onsets are the same table rows as the low band, order asserted, so misalignment is unlikely but not proven); per-sensor 306-ch envelopes (the 80 whitened comps span the band rank); >120 Hz; finer than 0.1 s bins or windows past 0.8 s; source-space/beamformed high-gamma; nonlinear/deep readers or the trunk on the continuous125 cache; other subjects. title: Lever: decomposed experts - acoustic / recognition / comprehension / timing / logic, each trained alone, stacked
description: Owner idea 2026-10-04: split the decision into independent experts so no expert can lean on another's easy cue. Evidence so far: post-hoc fusion of LDA (7gf.69) and the word head (7gf.76) gives nothing, because the context head already absorbs what the same inputs give. title: Lever: post-hoc per-member logit adjustment (Menon 2021) tuned on val
description: tau*log prior Fisher-consistent for balanced error. Check tau applied per member before averaging vs on ensemble. Zero GPU. Expected 0-1pt.
close_reason: Vacuous by algebra, no run. Ensemble.forward averages member log_softmax (model/ensemble.py:45); Evaluator.adjusted subtracts tau*log_prior then Sinkhorn-balances (scoring/evaluator.py:89). Subtraction is linear and log_softmax's per-row constant cannot change a row's ranking, so per-member tau_i before averaging == one ensemble tau = mean(tau_i): no new hypothesis space. Remaining knob is a finer tau grid than ADJUSTMENTS=(0,0.5,1) (score.py:16). Curve peaks near 0.5 (kdn2-s9 macro 0.551/0.582/0.482), so a 0.25/0.75 refinement is worth <~0.3pt and is tuned on the scored val itself. Not worth a slot. description: arXiv 2609.40359: joint sentence model hit 22.0% on no-brain synthetic vs 22.3% real via duration/IOI leakage. Our log-IOI carries that cue. Legit on holdout (onsets given) but sizes non-neural share of context gain -> where neural headroom is. Eval-only, minutes.

title: Lever: multi-latency word tokens from a continuous span feature map (deconvolve overlapping responses)
description: Words are 0.21 s apart (median), so a word's 1 s window holds the acoustic responses of the next ~4 words; the CNN pools each window into one vector, mixing them. Instead: run the CNN once over the whole span's continuous MEG, read the feature map at each word's onset + latencies (~0.1 acoustic, ~0.4 lexical, ~0.7 s late) as separate tokens tagged by latency; the transformer then attributes overlapping energy across words (a learned TRF deconvolution). Distinct from 2 s window (25.13), attention pool over time (45), TTA. Price: ~2-3 h code, 6 min/run; odds ~15% of +0.015. Pre-reg single seed >=0.632 (s0 0.617 + 1.5%) -> seeds; else directional.

title: Readout lever: per-class attention pooling over time/sensors (knee 'labelwise' analogue)
description: Knee-MRI session: past its plateau the biggest wins were aggregation (+0.054 ViT, 0.000 CNN: backbone-specific) and per-label pooling replacing a max head (which also reopened capacity). Our word encoder pools time/sensors into one embedding. Arm: replace the encoder's global pooling with per-class attention pooling (one learned query per class over the CNN time axis), behind an enum. Pre-reg: |delta| < 0.015 = null (expected: CNN analogue was flat in knee); > +0.015 = result, rerun 4 seeds. Run after maintenance epic h1u merges.
notes:
07:36Z design after reading wordnet.py:62-71: the CNN embed pools mean+max over 'segments' time chunks, then the transformer reads one vector per word and the class head comes only after mixing, so a literal per-CLASS query (1500+ classes x time) has no place before the transformer. Feasible analogue: Pooling enum {MEANMAX (default, byte-identical), ATTENTION(k queries over time, k*hidden -> same width)} in ConvConfig. Price: ~0.5h code after h1u.5 merges + ~1h/seed for 1 seed; plausible gain is small (knee CNN analogue 0.000), odds of clearing 1.5% about 15%. Run it as the cheap gap-filler only; the bigger lever is still speaker robustness (7gf.43: TheMoth is an unseen voice) and external data (7gf.44).
07:46Z arm running: sent40-ioi-attn-s0 = sent40-ioi-s0 config + --context.conv.queries 2 (AttentionPool, same width 512, MeanMax default has no params so old models load strictly). ~46 s/epoch, 40 ep. Compare to sent40-ioi-s0 0.6205 (rerun spread 0.003). Code uncommitted until h1u.5 merges (patch in scratchpad).
close_reason: NULL (pre-reg |d|<0.015): sent40-ioi-attn-s0 (2 attention queries, same width) macro 0.6146 vs sent40-ioi-s0 0.6205, n=2512 (Sherlock1 0.696 vs 0.704, TheMoth 0.539 vs 0.543). Kills 2-query attention readout on this CNN, not more queries or a per-sensor-group readout. Kept opt-in: --context.conv.queries. Side fact: a full 40-epoch sentence run takes ~6 min (9 s/epoch compiled).

title: Lexical aux: every heard word classified over the full lexicon
description: Mechanism: only 40% of heard words (307k/765k) carry a 50-way label; a softmax over every distinct heard token (Lexicon keys, ~25k) gives the other 60% a direct discriminative label (2.5x supervised windows). Differs from semantic aux (t5 SigLIP, null): CE over word identity, not alignment to a frozen embedding. Prior tempered by semantic+phoneme nulls. Pre-registered: single sent40-lex-s0 >= 0.627 (single mean 0.611 +0.015) -> keep, run 4-seed; 0.60-0.627 -> in band null; <0.60 -> hurts. Cost ~7 min/arm.

Mechanism fired: total loss 10.8->~8, the head learned identity over 25k words; no transfer to the 50-way ranking. Third every-word aux null after semantic (0.607) and phonetic: supervising the 60% unlabelled windows does not help this encoder. Not ruled out: a different weight (knob, priced below the bar), pretraining-then-finetune order.

title: TTA: average log-probs over window shifts (-1/0/+1 samples)
description: Test-time augmentation in Evaluator: each model's log-softmax averaged over window shifts in 50 Hz samples. Mechanism: onset alignment error plus ensemble-like averaging (ensembling transferred 3x to LB). No retraining. Pre-registered band: +0.003..+0.010 on n=2512 sentence-span novel macro vs ens-sent40-s0123 0.638; instrument, below 1.5% bar unless it surprises.
notes: 2026-10-03 04:05Z result: ens-sent40-s0123 --shifts -1 0 1 macro 0.6336 tau 0.5 n=2512 (Sherlock1 0.718, TheMoth 0.549) vs 0.638 no-TTA. Delta -0.004, below pre-registered band, inside noise. Not submitted. Mechanism read: +-20 ms is a full 50 Hz sample; members already average seed noise, and shifted reads move the onset-locked response off the alignment the model trained on, so averaging adds bias not variance reduction. Does NOT rule out sub-sample shifts or TTA with training-time jitter matched. Code kept (default shifts=(0,), opt-in).
close_reason: TTA +-1 sample null: 0.6336 vs 0.638 n=2512

title: Sentence encoder over the span's continuous MEG, conditioning the word encoder (FiLM / concat / cross-attention)
description: Owner idea 2026-10-06. Today each word reads a 1.0 s window from its onset through the word CNN, and the span transformer mixes only those word embeddings. Anything the word CNN discards (slow sentence-level state, per-sentence nuisance such as arousal, drift or a noise state, prosody) never reaches the model. Add a separate sentence encoder over the span's continuous MEG (sliced from the continuous run cache: small conv, then attention pool, giving s). Aggregation arms: (A) concat s onto each word embedding before the span transformer, cheapest; (B) FiLM: s gives gamma,beta modulating the word CNN's feature maps, a learned per-sentence adaptive normalisation (mechanism: a per-sentence nuisance distorts word responses multiplicatively or additively); (C) dense continuous encoder with word queries cross-attending to 10 Hz tokens (Perceiver-like), the largest change, and it also makes SSL natural (data2vec over long continuous stretches instead of 1 s windows, so 7gf.109.4 can pretrain the sentence encoder on 80 h). INSTRUMENT FIRST (minutes, CPU): from probs.pt (telemetry), test whether per-sentence accuracy is overdispersed against binomial at fixed per-word difficulty. If correctness clusters by sentence, a sentence-level state exists and B has a target; if not, A/B are near-null and only C's long-context route remains. Price: B ~4-6 h coding + ~1.5 h GPU per arm, ~10-15% odds of +1.5. Risk: the backbone already overfits, so the sentence branch must be small, with dropout on s. Test sets give spans (--grouping), so it is usable at inference.
notes: Owner 2026-10-06: it adds no new information (same MEG input). Agreed: its only value is inductive bias, i.e. retaining sentence-level state the word CNN discards and per-sentence normalisation. Demoted to P3; the build is gated entirely on the overdispersion instrument.

title: Lever: prior x evidence split - no-brain sequence prior + neural word likelihood combined as product of experts
description: From 7gf.71: the shuffled-MEG context model scores 0.521 vs 0.645 real (n=2512), so timing and sentence position carry ~0.32 of the 0.445 above chance. Suspicion: shortcut learning, where the easy prior lets the encoder under-learn the neural evidence. Instrument (cheap, eval-only, minutes): score log p_ctx + w * log p_wordhead, w picked on Sherlock1 and reported on TheMoth and the reverse; if the word head adds beyond the context head, the context head is under-using it. Lever (if the instrument shows room): train the encoder with PoE/residual loss (log prior from a frozen no-MEG timing model + neural logits, as in debiasing by product of experts, Clark et al. 2019 / He et al. 2019), so gradients go to what the prior cannot explain. Price ~2 h + 1 arm; odds of +0.015 ~20%. Not an LM-fusion submission: the prior is learned from training text and timing only.
notes: 2026-10-04 instrument on ens-kdn12 val logits (CPU cache from 7gf.69): context head (tau 0.5) + w * word head (tau 0/0.5/1), w in 0..1. Sherlock1 n=1296: base 0.7404, best 0.7440 (tau 0, w .05). TheMoth n=1216: base 0.5872, best 0.5925 (tau 1, w .1). Cross-picked: Sherlock1->TheMoth -0.0013, TheMoth->Sherlock1 -0.0061. Word-only top-10 hits 60 (S1) / 87 (Moth) vs context-only 271/306. The context head already uses the word head's evidence, so post-hoc re-weighting finds nothing. That kills the CHEAP post-hoc form only. PoE/residual TRAINING is untested, but its premise (that the neural channel is under-used) got no support here, so P3.

title: Lever: overlap deconvolution - subtract neighbours' word-agnostic evoked response (rERP)
description: Owner idea 2026-10-04 (hierarchical subtraction). Words ~0.21 s apart, response ~1 s: each window holds neighbours' responses. Word-agnostic part depends only on onsets (known on holdout, no labels) -> linear regression of MEG on onset-lagged impulses (Smith & Kutas 2015 rERP; Ehinger & Dimigen 2019 unfold), fit on train; subtract every OTHER word's predicted response from each word's window. Step 2 (later): word-specific templates weighted by model posteriors of neighbours, EM-like. Analytical front end; judge vs 25-seed mean 0.638 sd 0.005, bar 0.653; also as ensemble member.
notes: 2026-10-04 instrument (scratch, Deep subject-0 train 60k windows, word-agnostic TRF lags -0.1..2 s, same-sentence neighbours, mean 5.1/window, ridge sweep). First run on RAW cache units gave in-sample R2 1e-4 and negative val R2: harness bug, artefact outliers dominated the denominator (raw rms 65). On robust-scaled+centred windows (the model's view): in-sample R2 0.0013; val neighbour-term R2 at ridge 1e-3: Sherlock1 0.0015 (n=3427), TheMoth -0.0002 (n=2709), MOCHA 0.0010 (n=1748); full own+nb 0.0023/0.0000/0.0019. Context: grand onset-locked ERF = 0.04% of scaled window power (20x the 1/n floor), 1-4 Hz band 0.11%; word-specific ERF share ~1.5-2x its 1/n floor. So the generic neighbour response is REAL and of the same order as the word signal itself, but only ~0.1-0.2% of input variance, ~0 on TheMoth. Price: ~2-3 h (Windows-level subtraction + one arm), plausible gain <0.5% abs, odds of clearing 1.5% <10%. Downgraded P1->P3; not dead: re-test if a linear/LDA member (7gf.69) is built, where a fixed confound matters more than for the CNN.

title: Lever (priced): decode OOV word classes (length/POS) as LM context for in-vocab slots
description: From 7gf.53 close: a teacher-forced LM bound is unreachable because holdout neighbours are mostly OOV with unknown identity. Reachable variant: predict a coarse class per OOV slot (POS tag or word length, both learnable from MEG: length ~ duration/onset gap which is KNOWN from event onsets) and give a pretrained LM (or a POS n-gram over training text) the sequence of [in-vocab candidates + OOV class tokens]. Mechanism question: the span transformer already sees every word's MEG + onset spacing and learns word order from 765k training words (zero-MEG ctx 0.33), so the LM only adds what external text knows beyond that. Pricing: ~3-4 h code + ~1 h runs; plausible gain +0.005..+0.02, odds of clearing +0.015 ~15%. Cheap instrument first (~30 min): onset-gap features (word duration, gap to next) as explicit context inputs -- if the context model already exploits them, ablating them should cost >0.01; if it costs nothing, the OOV-class channel is unused and the lever has room.
